challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json kq records {"Ps.11.1": 1} — and Ps.11.1 is the ONLY K/Q ref anywhere in this cluster's six psalms (sweep: 1 K/Q verse across Ps 11-16, against 65 K/Q verses book-wide). Single-witness (WLC/OSHB). The boundary does not turn on which form is read, so this is a disclosure defect rather than a span defect — filed at low on that basis.

challenges.claim: The row places Psalm 11's 7 verses BOTH under and at the whole-psalm threshold, in the rationale and in observed_substrate_signals respectively.
challenges.evidence: The rationale reads "At 7 verses the psalm stays under the whole-psalm threshold"; observed_substrate_signals reads "the psalm totals 7 verses, at the whole-psalm threshold (sweep: 7 verses)". The book strategy §6 sets the whole-psalm class at roughly <=8 verses, so 7 is under it and the rationale is the correct member of the pair. This is the sole internal disagreement of its kind in the cluster: across the five whole_psalm rows the phrase resolves consistently everywhere else — 8 verses reads "at" in both fields, 6 verses reads "under" in both, 5 verses reads "under" in both (sweep: 5 whole_psalm rows, 9 occurrences of the threshold phrase, 1 row internally inconsistent). The neighbouring 7-verse psalm in this same cluster reads "under" in its rationale, corroborating that "under" is the correct reading for a 7-verse psalm.

Ps 12 is a shift+1 psalm and the row's arithmetic is correct: verse_map_web Ps.12.0 carries mt=Ps.12.1 with mt_title_verses=["Ps.12.1"], and I checked 8 of 8 body verses individually — web:Ps.12.V = oshb:Ps.12.V+1 throughout, so web:Ps.12.0 = oshb:Ps.12.1 is the 1 dual-cite the row owes (sweep: 1 of 8 refs), and it is correct. Every WEB quote verifies verbatim at its inline ref (sweep: 37 quotes across the cluster's 7 rows, 0 flags), the central oracle fragment included: “I will now arise,” says Yahweh sits at web:Ps.12.5 as claimed. Whole-psalm typing at 8 verses sits exactly at the strategy's roughly-<=8 class and is policy-compliant. One observation I decline to file: "the psalm totals 8 verses" is witness-dependent here — MT counts 9 because the title is MT v1 — and this is the only psalm in the cluster where the two witnesses disagree on the total; the toolkit's bare-ref convention resolves an unmarked count to WEB, so the row is covered.

challenges.claim: The row presents the Psalm 12 superscription as the ordered series "al-hashsheminit/lamnatseach/le-David", but the MT bytes run lamnatseach before al-hashsheminit.
challenges.evidence: Byte splice MT Ps.12.1 words[0:5] = לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל הַשְּׁמִינִ֗ית מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד (collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.12.1, tier byte; web:Ps.12.0 = oshb:Ps.12.1). Textual order is lamnatseach, then al-hashsheminit, then mizmor, then le-David; the row's slash-series inverts the first 2 of 4 labels. The series cannot be read as anything but textual order, because every other slash-series in this cluster (sweep: 3 of 3) follows the bytes: Ps 11 "lamnatseach/le-David" against MT Ps.11.1 words[0:2] = לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ לְדָ֫וִ֥ד, Ps 13 "lamnatseach/le-David" against MT Ps.13.1 words[0:3] = לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד, Ps 16 "miktam le-David" against MT Ps.16.1 words[0:2] = מִכְתָּ֥ם לְדָוִ֑ד (all tier byte) — sweep: 4 slash-series over titled opening rows in this cluster, 3 in byte order, 1 not. It matches no other authority either: psalm_device_inventory.json lists 12's labels as ["mizmor","lamnatseach","le_david","al_hashsheminit"]. Note the staged extract serializes maqaf as a space, so the two words after lamnatseach are one maqaf-joined unit in the pointed source and cannot be reordered around it.

reviews.reasoning: This row handles the book-central numbering hazard correctly, and I verified it against both witnesses rather than accepting it. The 13-split is real and symmetric in the data: verse_map_web gives Ps.13.5 mt=Ps.13.6 with mt_shared_with=["Ps.13.6"], and Ps.13.6 mt=Ps.13.6 with mt_shared_with=["Ps.13.5"], so both WEB verses render one MT verse, whose bytes open וַאֲנִ֤י בְּחַסְדְּךָ֣ בָטַחְתִּי֮ יָ֤גֵ֥ל (collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.13.6, tier byte). The row's paired dual-cites web:Ps.13.5 = oshb:Ps.13.6 and web:Ps.13.6 = oshb:Ps.13.6 are therefore the correct arithmetic, and citation_sweep.py accepts both against the split-aware rule. The title cite web:Ps.13.0 = oshb:Ps.13.1 conforms to the shift+1 mapping (Ps.13.0 mt=Ps.13.1, mt_title_verses=["Ps.13.1"]), and MT Ps.13.1 words[0:3] = לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד (tier byte) confirms the mizmor/lamnatseach/le-David labelling in byte order. I re-derived the fourfold claim instead of trusting it, in both witnesses independently: the MT skeleton query spliced from MT Ps.13.2 returns 2 occurrences in MT 13:2 and 2 in MT 13:3 — 4 occurrences over 2 verses, dual-citing web:Ps.13.1 = oshb:Ps.13.2 and web:Ps.13.2 = oshb:Ps.13.3 — and the independent WEB sweep of "how long" returns 2 occurrences at web:Ps.13.1 and 2 at web:Ps.13.2. Both witnesses agree, so the claim is true as stated. Treating the WEB 5|6 division as internal to the span is exactly right: it is a rendering seam with no Hebrew-verse boundary under it, and the device_notes correctly separates it from the typed cross-psalm relations rather than conflating the categories. Selah: no Ps.13 key in pmarks_Ps.json (sweep: 0 selah verses in Ps 13), none claimed. One observation recorded rather than filed: "fourfold" is a bounded occurrence count carried without an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its unit (4 occurrences over 2 verses, not 4 verses); the count is correct in both witnesses, so the defect is presentational and I decline to contest it.

The span, the whole-psalm typing and the decision to keep the 14/53 doublet as two rows under independent parents are all sound, and I contest none of them — merge/split across a typed doublet is out of scope in any case. Ps 14 is an identity psalm (Ps.14.0 mt="inside Ps.14.1", mt_title_verses empty), both witnesses run 7 verses, and the title bytes MT Ps.14.1 words[0:2] = לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ לְדָ֫וִ֥ד match the claimed lamnatseach/le-David in byte order. I re-derived every count the row carries and the numeric ones are right: the opening clause spliced from MT Ps.14.1 returns 2 verses book-wide — MT Ps.14.1 and MT Ps.53.2, i.e. web:Ps.14.1 and web:Ps.53.1 = oshb:Ps.53.2 — matching the row's "sweep: 2 verses"; the shorter clause returns 4 verses book-wide — MT 14:1, 14:3, 53:2, 53:4 = web:Ps.14.1, Ps.14.3, Ps.53.1, Ps.53.3 — matching the row's "4 verses book-wide" with its WEB refs exactly; the independent WEB sweeps agree (2 verses and 4 verses respectively). Selah: no Ps.14 key (sweep: 0 selah verses in Ps 14). Three defects follow: a verse argued but left uncited, a divergence claim that is false as written, and a grammatical mischaracterization of the divine name that works against the row's own warrant.

challenges.claim: The rationale argues Psalm 14:2's content — Yahweh's search from heaven — but attaches it to a web:Ps.14.3 citation and omits web:Ps.14.2 from boundary_evidence_refs, leaving 6 of the psalm's 7 verses cited.
challenges.evidence: The rationale reads "Yahweh's heavenly search finding ‘no one who does good, no, not one’ (web:Ps.14.3)". The quoted string reproduces web:Ps.14.3 exactly — “There is no one who does good, no, not one” — but the searching is the previous verse: “Yahweh looked down from heaven on the children of men” (web:Ps.14.2), whose bytes are MT Ps.14.2 words[0:3] = יְֽהוָ֗ה מִשָּׁמַיִם֮ הִשְׁקִ֪יף (collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.14.2, tier byte). Gloss and quote therefore cover different spans, against the standing rule that a quote span and its gloss cover the same span. boundary_evidence_refs lists web:Ps.14.0, 14.1, 14.3, 14.4, 14.5, 14.6 and 14.7 — 6 of the psalm's 7 verses, missing only 14.2 (sweep: 1 verse of 7 argued-but-uncited). check_refs_mirror.py returns GREEN on the row because the prose names no verse number at that point, so the mechanical arm cannot see it.

challenges.claim: device_notes states the doublet's wording "diverges at one point", naming just the fourth verse's divine name; the two psalms in fact diverge at all 6 parallel verse pairs, and the divine-name substitution alone stands at three of them.
challenges.evidence: Skeleton comparison of the MT parallels, pair by pair (Ps 53 is shift+1, so each 53 cite dual-cites): 14:1/53:2 differ in two words; 14:2/53:3 differ by the divine name alone — יְֽהוָ֗ה against אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים (both collate tier byte at oshb:Ps.14.2 and oshb:Ps.53.3; web:Ps.53.2 = oshb:Ps.53.3); 14:3/53:4 differ in their opening two words; 14:4/53:5 differ both by a quantifier and by the divine name — MT Ps.14.4 words[9:12] = יְ֝הוָ֗ה לֹ֣א קָרָֽאוּ against MT Ps.53.5 words[8:11] = אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א קָרָֽאוּ (tier byte; web:Ps.53.4 = oshb:Ps.53.5); 14:5 and 14:6 together stand against one MT verse, 53:6, which shares just its opening 3 words and then diverges wholesale, leaving MT Ps.14.6 = עֲצַת עָנִ֥י תָבִ֑ישׁוּ כִּ֖י יְהוָ֣ה מַחְסֵֽהוּ (tier byte) with no one-to-one counterpart at all; and 14:7/53:7 differ in two words including the divine name — בְּשׁ֣וּב יְ֭הוָה against בְּשׁ֣וּב אֱ֭לֹהִים (tier byte; web:Ps.53.6 = oshb:Ps.53.7). Divine-name substitution therefore stands at 3 parallel pairs (sweep: 3 pairs — MT 14:2/53:3, 14:4/53:5, 14:7/53:7 — plus 1 verse without a counterpart), not at one. psalm_device_inventory.json settles it with digits: Ps 14 carries 4 YHWH tokens against 3 Elohim, Ps 53 carries 0 YHWH against 7 Elohim, so Ps 53 contains 0 occurrences of the divine name the claim localizes to one verse. The row's own signal invokes Book I's Yahweh-dominant texture, so the texture is in view; only its extent is misstated.

challenges.claim: device_notes says Psalm 14's fourth verse "addresses Yahweh by name", but the divine name there is the object of the verb, not an addressee — and the row's own seam warrant turns on the absence of vocatives.
challenges.evidence: MT Ps.14.4 words[9:12] = יְ֝הוָ֗ה לֹ֣א קָרָֽאוּ (collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.14.4, tier byte): a third-person plural perfect under a negative particle, with the divine name as its object, not as an addressee. WEB renders it in the third person to match — “who eat up my people as they eat bread” stands in the same verse (web:Ps.14.4). No second-person form occurs in MT 14:4. Contrast a genuine vocative one psalm later: MT Ps.15.1 words[2:6] = יְ֭הֹוָה מִי יָג֣וּר בְּאָהֳלֶ֑ךָ (tier byte), where the divine name is addressed and the following noun carries a second-person suffix. The distinction is load-bearing here rather than cosmetic, because the row's rejected_alternative rests on "no imperative or vocative marking that seam" at the 4|5 seam — so describing 14:4 as an address undercuts the row's own warrant at exactly the verse the warrant depends on.

reviews.reasoning: I do not contest the span or the whole-psalm typing — Psalm 15 is a single question-and-answer movement and 5 verses is well inside the whole-psalm class. Ps 15 is an identity psalm (Ps.15.0 mt="inside Ps.15.1"), both witnesses run 5 verses, and the title bytes MT Ps.15.1 words[0:2] = מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥ד match the claimed mizmor/le-David in byte order (psalm_device_inventory.json labels for 15 = ["mizmor","le_david"]). The row's opening claim is byte-correct where it matters most: MT Ps.15.1 words[2:6] = יְ֭הֹוָה מִי יָג֣וּר בְּאָהֳלֶ֑ךָ (tier byte) is a true vocative with a following second-person suffix, so "a question addressed to Yahweh" is accurate. The English sweep is also accurate as an English sweep — WEB "he who" occurs at web:Ps.15.2, 15.3, 15.4 and 15.5 and not at web:Ps.15.1 (sweep: 4 of 5 verses, 5 occurrences, web:Ps.15.5 carrying 2). Selah: no Ps.15 key (sweep: 0 selah verses in Ps 15). The defect is that the non-split warrant is built on that English rather than on the source.

challenges.claim: The row's non-split warrant rests on "the relative ‘he who…’ construction" running continuously through verses 2-5, but that relative pronoun is supplied by WEB: MT Ps 15:2-5 contains 0 relative particles across its 4 verses and alternates participial with finite clauses.
challenges.evidence: The relative particle, spliced as a whole token from MT Ps.16.7, occurs in 94 verses book-wide but in 0 verses of MT Ps.15.1-5 (sweep: 0 verses in Ps 15; contrast 2 verses in the very next psalm, MT Ps.16.3 and MT Ps.16.7, both inside this cluster). The Hebrew alternates construction rather than sustaining one: MT Ps.15.2 words[0:4] = הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים וּפֹעֵ֥ל צֶ֑דֶק (collate tier byte) is participial, while MT Ps.15.3 words[0:4] = לֹֽא רָגַ֨ל עַל לְשֹׁנ֗וֹ (tier byte) is a negated finite perfect. WEB supplies its pronoun unevenly as well — web:Ps.15.4 opens “in whose eyes a vile man is despised”, not with the formula, which reaches that verse later at “he who keeps an oath even when it hurts” — so even the English is not the continuous construction the warrant describes. This is filed at medium rather than low because the rejected_alternative depends on it: the rival split of the catalog is dismissed because the construction "runs continuously without any independent imperative or vocative marker to justify a break", which dismisses a rival on WEB's syntax instead of the source's. The span is not contested, and a replacement warrant that passes the test this one fails is available in the source — an asyndetic qualification list, participial and finite by turns, answering the question put at web:Ps.15.1 = oshb:Ps.15.1 and closed by the verdict clause at web:Ps.15.5.

reviews.reasoning: The seam at 16:6|16:7 holds against both witnesses and against its rivals one verse either side, which is the test I applied rather than accepting the row's own account. Ps 16 is an identity psalm (Ps.16.0 mt="inside Ps.16.1"), MT and WEB both run 11 verses, so web:Ps.16.V = oshb:Ps.16.V throughout and the row's bare refs owe no dual-cite; the owner-ruled title cite web:Ps.16.0 = oshb:Ps.16.1 is correct. The title bytes MT Ps.16.1 words[0:2] = מִכְתָּ֥ם לְדָוִ֑ד (collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.16.1, tier byte) confirm miktam le-David in byte order, and the miktam count is exactly right — psalm_device_inventory.json genre_label_membership.miktam = [16, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60], so "1 of 6 miktam-titled psalms in the book (Psalms 16 and 56-60)" is accurate in number and in membership alike (sweep: 6 psalms). All six WEB quotes verify verbatim at their inline refs. The seam itself rests on source evidence stronger than the row claims for it: MT 16:5-6 closes a lexically bound portion-and-lot set, ending אַף נַ֝חֲלָ֗ת שָֽׁפְרָ֥ה עָלָֽי (tier byte), and MT 16:7 opens a new first-person verbal move, אֲבָרֵ֗ךְ אֶת יְ֭הוָה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצָ֑נִי (tier byte). I tested the rivals: a seam at 5|6 would split the portion/lot pair that shares its vocabulary, and a seam at 7|8 would strand the counsel line from the confession it governs, so neither carries a better tier-1 warrant than the one chosen. Selah: no Ps.16 key in pmarks_Ps.json (sweep: 0 selah verses in Ps 16), and none is claimed. The strophe split is policy-compliant at 6 and 5 verses, the parent is correct, and "medium" is honestly calibrated for a seam carried by lexical cohesion rather than by a frame or refrain.

All 5 WEB quotes verify verbatim at their inline refs (sweep: 5 quotes, 0 flags), and the row's disclosure hygiene is the best in the cluster. Ps 16 is an identity psalm, so the bare refs are correct with no dual-cite owed; the span closes the psalm at 16:11 and tiles exactly with its predecessor — check_tiling.py over Ps.11.1-Ps.16.11 returns 44 verses expected, 44 covered, 0 gaps and 0 overlaps across all seven rows. The selah claim is both true and correctly formed, which is the harder half: pmarks_Ps.json carries no Ps.16 key (sweep: 0 selah verses in Ps 16, against 71 book-wide), and the row scopes the absence to this strophe's span rather than asserting it globally, which is the span-scoping the standing rules require of an absence claim. Nothing else in the disclosure layer is owed here, and nothing is invented: the cluster's 1 K/Q verse sits at MT Ps.11.1 (sweep: 1 verse across Ps 11-16), the inverted nuns are confined to Ps 107 (sweep: 7 segs), and the book's 1 suspended letter is MT Ps.80.14. Paseq does fall at MT 16:9 and MT 16:10 per the inventory, and the row correctly makes no paseq claim rather than reaching for seg-layer corroboration. The cohesion warrant for verses 7-9 is sound and in fact understated: MT Ps.16.9 opens לָכֵ֤ן (collate tier byte), an inferential particle binding that verse back to 7-8, which argues continuity across the run the row describes rather than merely failing to divide it. Confidence "high" is calibrated, and the two-strophe arithmetic checks (11 verses as 6 and 5). One observation recorded rather than filed: "resurrection confidence" for 16:10 is an interpretive gloss rather than a source-level reading of the Hebrew, but it carries no weight in the seam and nothing in the row depends on it.
